subject: health
unitTitle: Body Systems, Hygiene, and Disease Prevention
title: Explicit model: germs and transmission
essentialQuestion: How can understanding body systems, hygiene, and disease prevention help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
keyPoints: Germs can spread through air, droplets, contact, food, water, or body fluids; prevention works by interrupting the relevant route rather than blaming a person who is ill.
Identify the actual biological process or transmission route, choose prevention or care that interrupts it, and correct myths without blaming or stigmatizing a person.
For germs and transmission, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Design an age-appropriate prevention routine and explain when adult help is required.
studentTask: Create a cause-and-interruption map for a supplied fictional case about germs and transmission: name the relevant process or transmission route, add two accurate prevention or care supports, and correct one misconception using the lesson facts.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in germs and transmission; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the germs and transmission task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
